findings.heading: Prepare table / Подготовка таблицы
findings.proposition: The Russian section opens with an extra paragraph announcing the Descriptive-tables example that builds `table`; the English has that announcement only once, after the '*Before* beginning' instruction paragraph, and the Russian repeats it again at line 158.
findings.reader_consequence: The Russian reader meets the example announcement, then the prerequisite instruction, then the same announcement again, and cannot tell whether two different examples or two different `table` objects are being described.

findings.heading: Prepare table / Подготовка таблицы
findings.proposition: The English sends the reader to the Descriptive tables and Pivoting data pages with working links (tables_descriptive.qmd, pivoting.qmd); the Russian keeps the label text but drops both link destinations, so '[Описательные таблицы]' and '[Поворот данных]' carry no target.
findings.reader_consequence: The Russian reader sees bracketed page names that do not resolve to anything and has no route to the two pages that teach how to build the data frame flextable requires.

findings.heading: Create a flextable / Создать flextable
findings.proposition: The English gives the accepted values of `part = ` as the literal strings "header", "body" and "all"; the Russian gives them as "заголовок", "тело" and "все", which are not values flextable accepts and do not appear in any code chunk on the page.
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader following the syntax description writes part = "заголовок" and the flextable call fails, with nothing in the surrounding prose to show which spelling is correct.

findings.heading: Borders and background / Границы и фон
findings.proposition: The English instructs the reader to specify `part = ` as either "all", "body" or "header" for hline() and vline(); the Russian instructs "все", "тело" or "заголовок", which contradicts the chunk beside it at lines 309-327 where the argument is written part = "all".
findings.reader_consequence: A Russian reader copies the translated value into hline() or vline() and the border is never drawn, while the adjacent code shows a different spelling and the text does not explain the discrepancy.
